events.text:
🇬🇧🛰 Britain touts new space warfare unit
The so-called No. III Space Effects Squadron is the British Royal Air Force’s first unit dedicated to protecting UK satellites.
While No. I Space Operations Squadron and No. II Space Warning Squadron are tasked with detecting potential space threats, No. III Squadron is expected to act on these warnings and deal with the threats using “advanced technology, including electronic warfare,” the British government said in a press release.
➡️Earlier this month, the UK pledged £274 million (about $364 million) to bolster the country’s “apace domain awareness” in order to keep a better track satellites, rockets and space debris.
This initiative comes as Western powers ramp up their military spending under the pretext of countering some unspecified threat posed by Russia and China.
Britain has also doubled down on its military cooperation with the US, though it remains to be seen how the new UK space squadron might interact with the US Space Force.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🇺🇸🛩 US braces for Ukraine-trained cartel drone operators to enter drug war
Narco-terrorists returning from Ukraine will “almost certainly” undermine Donald Trump’s war on drugs across the Western Hemisphere, The Washington Post reports.
The Ukraine conflict alumni, chiefly from Colombia, boast skills and tactics involving the use of modern drone models and the evasion of electronic warfare systems. Those skills are expected to be adopted by drug cartels in the coming months, US officials say. The pipeline of expertise is unlikely to dry up, as cartels are sending new recruits to Ukraine on one-year contracts to stay up-to-date with drone warfare technology.
Drug lords in Mexico have already employed unmanned vehicles to monitor the US-Mexico border, monitor US enforcement operations, and identify better smuggling routes. At least one cartel has a hexacopter or octocopter capable of staying airborne for hours and carrying a payload of around 70 kg. This trend is leaving US and Mexican counternarcotics authorities “dangerously unprepared” for a standoff with battle-tested "droneros" deployed by the cartels.
The US government is reportedly aware of the looming crisis and has raised it with Kiev, which continues to welcome Latin American mercenaries amid a troop shortage and Western pressure to sustain the war.
